entries.reason: only the authorization of the library is carried, answered from the ALAssetsLibrary of the release, whose status and prompt are the same photo permission; the rest of the class needs the Photos database that iOS 6 does not have
entries.effect: +sharedPhotoLibrary gives one object; +authorizationStatus is the ALAssetsLibrary status as PHAuthorizationStatus (not determined, restricted, denied, authorized); +requestAuthorization: shows the system prompt when the status is not determined, by reading the saved-photos group, and calls the handler off the main thread with the new status, and calls it with the current status when it is already decided
entries.source: Photos of the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0: +[PHPhotoLibrary authorizationStatus] at 0x18fbafb5c reads the Photos TCC status and its restricted flag, +requestAuthorization: at 0x18fbafc7c asks the shared privacy object; an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 for the status the release's ALAssetsLibrary gives

entries.reason: the same status for both access levels: iOS 6 has no limited access, so it is never PHAuthorizationStatusLimited

entries.reason: changes are made through ALAssetsLibrary, which can add an image or a video to the saved photos and nothing else
entries.effect: the block is run and its requests are checked and then written, one after another; the completion handler is called once off the main thread with the success and an error of PHPhotosErrorDomain; a change that deletes or edits fails as a whole before anything is written
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; the host's Photos for the defaults, constants and exception text; an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 and the iOS 6.0 emulator for what ALAssetsLibrary gives and the release does not export
